CallKit engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume CallKit capability covers storefront language. Xcode, Developer portal, and Connect actually separate call behavior from product-page copy:

  • CallKit & CXProvider — configured in your app to report incoming and outgoing calls to the system. Controls whether calls appear on the native call screen. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • PushKit VoIP push — server payloads and token registration for incoming call alerts. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains call UI value to buyers.
  • In-app call UI & caller ID strings — labels on the native incoming-call interface and in-call controls. Your listing may mention native call UI; implementing CallKit handlers is engineering work, not listing copy.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of CallKit flags in the binary.

Working CallKit in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Call-centric apps often lead marketing screenshots with native incoming-call UI or lock-screen answer mockups — surfaces where English system chrome and your marketing blurbs appear together:

  • English title and subtitle — app name and tagline still Latin script while competitors show native Chinese call positioning
  • Untranslated CallKit badges — overlay lines like "Native call UI", "Incoming call", "System call screen", or "Works with CallKit" remain English on zh-Hans gallery frames

  • Keyword field still en-US — buyers search 来电显示, 原生通话界面, VoIP通话, or 系统来电界面; an English-only keyword row misses China Search intent

  • Over-claiming in machine translation — stiff 翻译腔 that implies you replace the built-in Phone app, provide cellular service, or are a carrier when your app is VoIP-only

Better zh-Hans listing copy helps call-aware buyers understand native UI value before install. It does not replace CallKit engineering, in-app caller ID strings, or Apple's review decisions — and it must not claim PSTN or carrier replacement.

CallKit-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Call-centric listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe native call UI — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Native call screen vs generic "calls"

US pages use "Native call UI", "System incoming call", or "Answer on the lock screen." Chinese buyers expect concise 原生通话界面, 系统来电界面, or 像电话一样接听 phrasing rather than English slogans left on screenshot overlays — without implying you are the built-in Phone app or a mobile carrier.

VoIP scope without carrier or PSTN claims

Description and caption lines should name the call types your app actually supports — in-app VoIP, team voice, customer callback — without promising cellular replacement, unlimited PSTN minutes, or features your backend does not support. AppLocale rewrites from your English claims; we do not invent telephony behavior.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need call-relevant search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 来电, VoIP, and 通话界面 each signal different intent from generic messaging keywords.

Screenshot captions on call-screen frames

Gallery frames that show the native incoming-call interface, lock-screen answer UI, or Recents-style call history need one-line zh-Hans captions — "VoIP来电，系统原生接听界面" not "Native call UI" burned into the product page story.

Common mistakes on CallKit zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming CallKit setup localizes automatically — CallKit integrated in Xcode; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and call-screen screenshot caption lines still English
  • Calling VoIP "phone replacement" — 替代电话 or 取代系统电话 overclaims when the app is in-app VoIP only
  • Implying carrier or PSTN service — listing claims unlimited cellular calls when the app uses internet VoIP only
  • Conflating listing copy with in-app caller ID strings — CXCallUpdate localized names and in-call labels are binary localization, not Connect metadata
  • English "Incoming call" on zh-Hans screenshots — Connect caption fields are Chinese but burned-in call mockups on PNG exports are still Latin
  • What's New still English after CallKit launch — see What's New in Simplified Chinese when native call UI shipped in a recent version
  • Expecting AppLocale to configure CallKit or PushKit — CXProvider, VoIP push tokens, and server payload work are outside listing rewrite

Listing copy should describe in-app VoIP or messaging calls that use Apple's native incoming-call interface — without implying you replace the built-in Phone app, provide PSTN cellular service, or are a carrier. CallKit listing copy covers native incoming-call UI and system call-screen marketing — not generic push alert permission prompts, not Live Activities on Dynamic Island, and not SharePlay shared sessions. Those surfaces have separate listing guides.

No. The native incoming-call interface, caller ID labels, and in-call controls come from your app binary and CallKit configuration — not App Store Connect listing fields. AppLocale covers product-page marketing copy only.
